# IC Memo Drafting

⚠️ **Finance warning / Avertissement finance** : informational only, not investment advice. A well-drafted memo is an argument, not a guarantee: the investment it recommends can still lose money, private equity carries a real risk of loss, and no return figure here is a promise of return. Curated by Skill Harbor: the IC memo drafting skill of the private equity pack in andreworia/claude-finance-skills. Use it after diligence is substantially complete and the deal team has formed a clear view; the memo is the written case for or against the decision and must survive cross-examination from senior investment professionals, LPs and risk committees, with no material diligence finding omitted. The method drafts nine sections and writes the executive summary last, because its thesis and risk statements must reflect what the body actually demonstrates: a one-page summary stating the company, the deal (structure, entry multiple, implied EV, equity cheque), the thesis in three bullets, the primary risk and its mitigant in one, the recommendation, and the base-case MOIC and IRR. The body covers a factual business description in plain language (what it does, who buys it, how it is sold, revenue model, scale, history, with no marketing copy), market and competitive position in two to three paragraphs drawn from the commercial workstream, deal overview (process, seller motivation, structure, leverage and tranches, conditions and use of proceeds), and a direct management assessment (track...
